gloss: to have a keen nose; to sniff out; to be shrewd at detecting

definitions.gloss: to have a keen nose; to sniff out; to be shrewd at detecting opportunities or information
definitions.explanation: To use one's intuition or shrewdness to detect something, especially business opportunities, trends, or information that others miss. A figurative expression using the nose as a metaphor for intuition.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はビジネスに{鼻|はな}を{利|き}かせる。
examples.english: He has a keen nose for business.

examples.japanese: {記者|きしゃ}は{鼻|はな}を{利|き}かせて{特|とく}ダネを{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: The reporter sniffed out a scoop.

examples.japanese: {流行|りゅうこう}に{鼻|はな}を{利|き}かせて、いつも{新|あたら}しい{商品|しょうひん}をいち{早|はや}く{仕入|しい}れる。
examples.english: With a keen nose for trends, they always stock new products ahead of everyone else.

notes:
A figurative expression where {鼻|はな} (nose) represents intuition or the ability to detect something. The idiom implies shrewdness and the ability to sense opportunities or important information before others.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ビジネスに{鼻|はな}を{利|き}かせる: to have a nose for business
- {流行|りゅうこう}に{鼻|はな}を{利|き}かせる: to sniff out trends
- {情報|じょうほう}に{鼻|はな}を{利|き}かせる: to be shrewd about information

RELATED WORDS:
- {鼻|はな}が{利|き}く: to have a keen sense of smell; to be shrewd (intransitive version)
- {嗅覚|きゅうかく}が{鋭|するど}い: to have a sharp sense of smell — can be literal or figurative
- {目|め}が{利|き}く: to have a good eye — parallel expression using sight instead of smell
